description: Ocean's Eye aims to make ocean data easier to discover, understand and use. We're working toward one map for exploring public marine gridded data, searching in plain language and accessing useful data through clear, configurable endpoints. Starting with marine life and the environmental patterns around it, we want to help researchers, fishermen, companies and curious explorers make sense of the ocean.
summary: Ocean's Eye puts public ocean data on one map and lets anyone ask about it in plain language. Search a species and the map shows where it has been reported (OBIS records, which show reported presence, not abundance). Switch on NASA satellite layers for sea-surface temperature, anomaly, chlorophyll-a and currents, plus wave and weather models and depth relief. Tap any ocean point for a briefing that names each source, resolution and time. An AI assistant is instructed to answer from the app's own live data routes and cite the dataset and time; it can still err, so check the sources. If a source is down, the app says so instead of estimating. It is a prototype for exploration, not a safety forecast, and was built with AI assistance.
details:
Ocean's Eye is an interactive web map that brings public ocean data together and helps people explore it through maps and plain-language questions.

Users can search for a marine species and see where it has been reported through OBIS occurrence records. Map layers include NASA GIBS sea-surface temperature, temperature anomaly, chlorophyll-a and ocean-current imagery, GEBCO depth relief, and Open-Meteo modelled wave heights. Selecting an ocean location opens a briefing with available ocean and weather conditions, their sources and timestamps. A Data & API catalog explains the data routes and their upstream sources.

The built-in AI assistant is instructed to answer using the app's data tools and cite the dataset and valid time. A keyword-based helper is available without an AI model. AI answers can still be wrong and should be checked against their sources.

The intended benefit is to reduce the effort needed for students, researchers and fishers to find and understand marine information. The creative approach is to connect marine-life reports with satellite and model layers in one interface, rather than requiring users to move between separate portals.

We built the prototype using JavaScript, Leaflet and Node.js, with public data APIs and an optional OpenAI-compatible language model. AI tools assisted with coding, debugging, research, writing, presentation preparation and an illustrative Gemini-generated animation. No specialised hardware is required to use the web interface.

We considered accessibility for non-specialists, source attribution, data age, resolution, uncertainty and service availability. OBIS records show reported presence, not abundance. Some current imagery is stale and is labelled accordingly. Wave and weather values are model outputs, and trend results are indicative rather than proof. External services such as NOAA ERDDAP may be unavailable, so coverage is not guaranteed.

Ocean's Eye is a prototype for exploration and learning, not a validated navigation or safety forecast.
